Wisconsin Creative · September 28, 2026

Scoreboard: web + native iOS

An end-to-end pass through presentation, navigation, counting, API contracts, and recovery. Changes are local and uncommitted.

Web layout and history

Same existing isolated Preview dataset, authenticated hidden Admin, route, viewport, appearance and fixed capture clock. Synthetic names are expected. Source manifests and hash-bound receipts are retained.

Context and recovery · after-only

These exact workflow states do not have a trustworthy matching baseline. Web failures use controlled HTTP responses over an authenticated local session; native states use the isolated fixture API.

What changed, and why

Team context survives navigation

Was

Individual reads dropped venue/opponent; native navigation also dropped the selected team stack.

Now

All four dimensions carry into the person view. Stable season facets and Clear filters keep the explorer switchable.

Records and history have distinct rules

Was

Result-less work could disappear, raw-title NULL comparisons could omit manual official games, and page-sized history truncated streaks.

Now

Two bounded scalar reads separate completed work from official results. Full-season recent results/streaks are computed before paging; exclusions, ties and count-once participation remain server-owned.

Failure preserves useful context

Was

Failed filter changes could reset controls or hide why old numbers remained.

Now

Both clients retain the last loaded scope, keep requested controls selected, and explain Retry. Obsolete pages are rejected; duplicate IDs merge once.

Native paper cuts

Was

All-day dates could fall into the prior local day, and invalid cursors could repeat page one.

Now

Calendar-day labels are stable, non-advancing cursors stop paging, names accompany person navigation, and team search retains rank.

Verification

  • 123 focused web/API/source-contract tests passed across 13 files.
  • 3 Scoreboard checks passed against disposable local PostgreSQL, alongside 8 existing custody checks. Covers actual SQL NULL semantics, exclusions, hidden identities, canonical filtering, paging and team/profile/person agreement.
  • 17 native model tests and 3 native UI workflows passed on the required iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator. Xcode builds passed for Wisconsin and WisconsinPerformance.
  • Authenticated Preview checks passed for navigation, filtered work counts, validation, stale-data retry, clearing, search, and tablet/phone overflow. Controlled HTTP fixtures verified failed pagination, deduplication and terminal cursors; browser page errors: 0.
  • TypeScript, changed-file lint, app-only production build, docs verification and diff checks passed. No schema changes or migrations were run against a shared database.
  • Repository-wide lint remains blocked by the existing no-assign-module-variable error in public/qrcode/vendor/jsQR.js; changed files are clean. Existing unrelated lint warnings remain.

Things to know

  • The after-only gallery has no matching baseline for its exact workflow states; it is not a before/after comparison.
  • No ESPN integration exists or was added. Results still come from Wisconsin calendar markers; work participation comes from Schedule assignments and recorded workers.
  • No commit, push, deployment or distribution was performed. Production Student/Collaborator reads, authenticated native totals and regular-width iPad acceptance remain GAP-71.
